[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted** [LC 167 · Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted](https://leetcode.com/problems/two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted/){difficulty="Medium"}

Two Sum (@sec-hash-p1-a) needed a hash map because the array was *unordered* — the partner of $x$ could be anywhere. Here the array is **sorted**, so the answer has structure: if $a[\mathit{lo}] + a[\mathit{hi}]$ is too small, the only way to raise it is to grow the left term, and if it is too big, the only way to lower it is to shrink the right term. One of the two ends can be thrown away with certainty at every step, so a single $\mathit{lo}/\mathit{hi}$ squeeze answers the question in one pass and $O(1)$ memory — no map needed.

[Solved in full in @sec-tp-p1-a.]{.card-link}

:::
